🌟 nyx | Shell
🎯 Primary Use Case: Obscuring digital forensic traces on user systems.
✨ Key Features: • Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS, Windows) • Comprehensive artifact cleaning modules
📖 Summary: Nyx is a self-contained shell script designed to clean forensic traces across Linux, macOS, and Windows operating systems. It systematically removes various artifacts left by user activity, applications, and system processes to help obscure digital footprints.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 Constrict | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Compressing video files to meet specific size limits for uploads or storage, without manual trial-and-error.
✨ Key Features: • Compress videos to target file sizes • Automatic calculation of ABR, resolution, framerate, and audio quality • Bulk compression • Customizable framerate limits • Choice of codecs (H.264, HEVC, AV1, VP9)
📖 Summary: Constrict is a desktop application for Linux that allows users to compress video files to a target file size. It automatically calculates the necessary encoding parameters like bitrate, resolution, and framerate to achieve the desired output size while aiming to preserve audiovisual quality.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 claude-code-karma | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a user-friendly, visual interface for monitoring and analyzing their Claude Code sessions locally, offering insights into session activity, tool usage, and agent interactions.
✨ Key Features: • Local-first dashboard for Claude Code sessions • Visualizes sessions, timelines, costs, and live activity • Reads directly from `~/.claude/` data • Session Browser with search and filtering
📖 Summary: Claude Code Karma is a local-first, open-source dashboard designed to visualize and monitor Claude Code sessions. It transforms raw session data from `~/.claude/` into an interactive timeline, session browser, and detailed overviews of tasks, files, subagents, and skills invoked during a session.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 thedeck | Dart
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a digital, cooperative platform for playing classic card games on mobile devices, with a shared visual interface.
✨ Key Features: • Cross-platform mobile support (Android, iOS) • Built with Flutter and Dart • Unique 'table' device feature for shared gameplay • Supports classic card games • Offline multiplayer capabilities
📖 Summary: The Deck is an open-source, cross-platform mobile card game engine built with Flutter. It allows users to play classic card games digitally, with a unique feature where one device acts as a shared 'table' visible to all players, enhancing cooperative gameplay.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ dashy | Vue
🎯 Primary Use Case: To serve as a customizable, self-hosted homepage or dashboard for managing and monitoring personal homelab services and applications.
✨ Key Features: • Multiple pages support • Real-time status monitoring • Widgets for dynamic content • Instant search and customizable shortcuts • Theming with UI color editor and custom CSS
📖 Summary: Dashy is a highly customizable, self-hostable personal dashboard designed for managing and monitoring your homelab services. It offers features like real-time status checks, customizable widgets, theming, icon options, and optional authentication, making it an ideal startpage or homepage for tech enthusiasts.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 ailia-models | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide developers with easy access to a wide range of pre-trained AI models that can be readily integrated into applications using the ailia SDK, simplifying the deployment of AI functionalities.
✨ Key Features: • Collection of 400+ pre-trained AI models • Supports diverse AI tasks (object detection, speech recognition, image generation, LLMs, etc.) • Single, simple CLI for all models
📖 Summary: The ailia-models repository provides a comprehensive collection of over 400 pre-trained AI models for various tasks, including object detection, speech recognition, image generation, and LLMs. These models are designed to be easily runnable from a single command-line interface and are compatible with the ailia SDK across multiple platforms.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
